earlier_scan.note: Glottolog lists Latala as unclassifiable with no descriptive references; no documentation found.

sources.citation: ELDP projects list (eldp.net): entries 'Basa Latala, Indonesia, Luigi Sausa, 2026' and 'Sajau, Indonesia, Luigi Sausa, 2026'; ELAR collection page SO_64651d6d-0253-41f9-91c2-8e7a8a7fad1d
sources.note: Confirms the only documentation project on Basa Latala is the 2026 ELDP pilot; no outputs beyond the collection guide.

sources.citation: Kusuma, P. 2023. Mengenal 3 keunikan suku Punan Batu untuk memahami evolusi manusia dan pola migrasi di Kalimantan. The Conversation Indonesia, 5 Dec 2023. doi:10.64628/aan.3qjtrc3f6
sources.note: Popular piece: Latala is 'bahasa lagu.. yang tidak memiliki hubungan secara linguistik dengan bahasa lain di Kalimantan'; mentions 'penggunaan nada yang bervariasi (dengan menira, atau bernyanyi)' -- melodic variation in singing, not word stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid lata1235 (page, JSON, and GitHub md.ini) plus reference records 674493 and 690421
sources.note: No descriptive work at all: only two 'a wordlist or less' references (Lansing et al. 2022, listed by Glottolog as an ethnographic work;wordlist; Blevins & Kaufman 2024, listed by Glottolog as a comparative study;wordlist). Altnames 'Latala Song language', 'Latala ancestral language of this group of Punan Batu'. The earlier scan's 'no descriptive references' reflected Glottolog 5.1, which listed nothing.

sources.citation: Sausa, Luigi (depositor). Documenting Sajau and Basa Latala: Everyday and Ritual Languages of the Punan Batu in North Kalimantan, Borneo. ELDP SG1218 / ELAR deposit 0850 (pilot June-Oct 2026; planned IPA transcription tier, Register tier, FLEx lexicon), status Forthcoming; plus any phonology sketch or report Sausa produces from it
sources.note: The first and only documentation project on Basa Latala; its IPA-tier recordings and any resulting sketch are the first place a stress/prosody statement for Latala could appear. As of the 17 June 2026 collection guide nothing phonological exists yet.

sources.citation: Sausa, Luigi. 2026. Metadocumentation_0850 (collection guide, 17 June 2026). In: Documenting Sajau and Basa Latala: Everyday and Ritual Languages of the Punan Batu in North Kalimantan, Borneo. ELDP SG1218, ELAR deposit 0850 (status Forthcoming; pilot June-Oct 2026). hdl:2196/84ba14d9-ceec-4527-a7ae-eb507a2c6f8c
sources.note: Nothing on stress or prosody. Basa Latala is coded qaa-x-latala and labelled the 'ritual register'; the ELAN template has an IPA tier; the phoneme inventory (a i u e̞ ə o̞ + 19 consonants) is 'a preliminary working inventory (a starting point based on the closest documented Bornean Austronesian language, Iban)'. The metadocumentation is the only open item; no recordings or lexicon deposited yet (re-checked collection page 2026-09-17).

sources.citation: Prasetijo, A. 2025. Orang Punan Batu Benau Sajau: Kesinambungan Hunter-Gatherer dan Warisan Budaya Karst di Kalimantan Utara. JANUS (UGM). doi:10.22146/janus.24362
sources.note: Anthropology of subsistence, mobility and cosmology; does not discuss the Latala language.

sources.citation: Kusuma, P., et al. 2023. Deep ancestry of Bornean hunter-gatherers supports long-term local ancestry dynamics. Cell Reports 42(11): 113346. doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2023.113346 (open access, PMC7618103)
sources.note: Nothing; one sentence: 'they also preserve a unique song language (the Latala language, or Menirak ("to sing")) that is unrelated to any existing languages in the region.'

sources.citation: Lansing et al. 2022, Supplementary Information S2513843X22000032sup001.docx, section 'Supplementary Methods and Results on Linguistics'
sources.note: Nothing. Discusses only elicitation differences between the two Basa Latala lists ([luwai] vs [paluwai] 'to say', [majaN] vs [bajaN] 'child', [lakopan] vs [parakopan] 'to know') and manual cognate counts (Table S3). Zero hits for stress/accent/phonolog/syllab/vowel.

sources.citation: Lansing, J. S., G. S. Jacobs, S. S. Downey, P. K. Norquest, M. P. Cox, S. L. Kuhn, J. H. Miller, S. G. Malik, H. Sudoyo & P. Kusuma. 2022. Deep ancestry of collapsing networks of nomadic hunter-gatherers in Borneo. Evolutionary Human Sciences 4: e9, 1-19. doi:10.1017/ehs.2022.3 (open access, PMC10426063)
sources.note: Nothing. Latala named 22 times: 'a hitherto undocumented language which is not spoken, but rather sung, customarily at night in the rock shelters or caves. This song language, Latala or Menirak ("to sing" in the daily Punan language), is known only to the Punan Batu'; called 'a language isolate' on lexicostatistical grounds; 130-item Swadesh lists 'transcribed into the International Phonetic Alphabet'. Zero hits for stress/accent/prosod/syllab/penult.

sources.citation: Lansing, J. S. et al. 2020. Punan comparative language data.xlsx (Norquest's IPA 200-item Swadesh lists incl. column 'Basa Latala'). Figshare dataset. doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.12466001
sources.note: 130 Basa Latala forms in broad IPA (aku, kajuŋ, kaniku, palikaban, paɟituke, dariasal, taumenditawena..): no stress marks on any form, no prose; the only bare wordlist in existence.

sources.citation: Blevins, Juliette & Daniel Kaufman. 2024. Austronesian lexemes in Basa Latala of Borneo: a Punan Sajau song language. Oceanic Linguistics 63(1): 182-201.

sources.note: The only linguist-authored paper on Basa Latala (a phonologist's reanalysis of the Lansing/Norquest wordlist); might include remarks on syllable/word shape or prosody of the song forms, though it works from a list without stress marks. Must be read to close the question.
